title: Count the Number of K-Big Indices
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums and a positive integer k, identify indices i that are k-big.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums and a positive integer k, identify indices i that are k-big. An index i is k-big if there are at least k indices idx1 i with nums[idx2] < nums[i]. Return the count of such k-big indices.
constraints: An index is k-big when at least k earlier and k later values are strictly smaller than its value.
Equal values do not count as smaller.
Return the number of k-big indices.
hints: Process each index while maintaining frequency structures for values to its left and right.
Coordinate-compress values and use prefix sums through rank minus one to count strictly smaller values.
Remove the current value from the right tree, query both trees, then add it to the left tree.
The two Fenwick trees represent exactly the earlier and later indices at every step, so both threshold checks match the definition.
